Mass notify / email Pessimistic or Undo Send window External irreversibility
AI mutate file / send Diff → apply → undo (Ch. 14) Silent mutation destroys trust

Case A — Checkout: pessimistic; field errors; receipt. Reject optimistic “Paid!” before bank. Measure payment success, error recovery, keyboard completion, chargebacks.

Case C — Shared destructive delete: confirm with blast radius or Trash 30d if recoverable. Reject soft toast for team-visible destroy. Focus trap + announced result + restore focus to trigger.

10.9 Chapter 10 summary

  • Acknowledge ≤100ms; tier the wait; never blank the page for a click.
  • Classify every mutation: soft / quarantine / hard.
  • Design the seven states; then specialize empty vs zero vs error vs denied with distinct copy and CTAs.
  • Optimistic when rollback is cheap; pessimistic on money, legal, and shared blast.

Forms & auth playbook (expanded)

Concern Rule
Labels Visible always; never placeholder-as-label
Validation Blur for format; submit for required set; preserve input on error
Errors Field-local + optional GOV.UK Error Summary (linked list)
Layout Trust paths = 1-column; paired short fields may 2-col on wide CQ
Double-submit Disable + in-place pending; idempotent keys on pay/create-once
Auth autocomplete correct; passkeys/OTP > passwords alone; PM-friendly
CAPTCHA Accessible alternative always (Case F); no puzzle-only
Session Warn before timeout; extend; restore drafts where safe

Typeahead / combobox: Prefer native <datalist> or full APG combobox (arrow keys, typeahead, aria-activedescendant). Don’t fake autocomplete with divs.

Offline matrix:

Mode UI
Read-only offline Banner; disable mutating controls with explanation
Queue offline Banner “changes queued”; syncing state on flush
Conflict Keep both / choose / merge prefer-when (Ch 14)

Chapter 11 — Search, Filter, Sort & Pagination

Finding work is half of product interaction. Cmd-K is a power palette—not a substitute for a search product. This chapter covers the information-seeking kit flagged as a critical gap: query, scope, empty/zero results, ranking honesty, faceted refine, URL persistence, and pagination vs infinite scroll vs load-more.

11.1 Findability system map

Surface Job Typical entry
Global search / Cmd-K Jump to object or action Keyboard; spotlight
In-place search Narrow current list Search field above list/table
Filters / facets Constrain by attributes Chips, sidebar, sheet
Sort Order by relevance or field Column header / select
Pagination / scroll Traverse the result set Pager, load more, infinite

Treat these as one system: changing search, filter, or sort should update the same result region, the same URL (when shareable), and the same zero-state recovery.

11.2 Search product requirements

Cmd-K ≠ search product. A complete search experience needs:

  1. Query — what the user typed; visible; clearable.
  2. Scope — where we look (this project, all projects, people, files, actions). Default scope must be obvious.
  3. Results — ranked list with type labels; keyboard navigation; open on Enter.
  4. Empty query state — recent, suggested, or actions—not a blank void.
  5. Zero results — honest “No matches for query”; offer clear search, change scope, or spelling help—not popular items disguised as matches.
  6. Ranking honesty — do not silently rewrite the query; if you fall back (e.g. stem, fuzzy), say so.
  7. Error / denied — distinct from zero (Ch. 10 taxonomy).
  8. Performance — acknowledge keystroke; debounce network; show pending without layout thrash.

Steal: Linear Cmd-K for action+object jump; keep a progressive path for users who never learn the shortcut (visible Search in chrome).

11.3 Filter & faceted refine

Pattern Prefer when Notes
Chip filters Few active dimensions; always visible Removable chips; “Clear all”
Filter sheet (mobile) Many facets; small viewport Apply/Cancel; show count preview
Sidebar facets Desktop power tools; high density Sticky; URL-synced
Inline column filters Tables with known columns Don’t hide behind mystery icons only

Rules:

  • Active filters must be visible—never invisible constraints.
  • Filtered-to-zero uses Clear filters CTA (Ch. 10.7).
  • Show result count when filters change (“12 of 480”).
  • Persist filters in the URL for shareable/deep-linkable views unless privacy forbids (then session storage + explicit “Save view”).
  • Facet counts should not lie: if a facet would yield zero given current selection, disable or show 0—don’t offer dead ends without signal.

11.4 Sort

  • Default sort must match user expectation (often recent activity or relevance under search).
  • Column-header sort: indicate direction; support keyboard; announce change politely.
  • Multi-sort only when power users need it—and show the sort order explicitly.
  • Sorting under an active search: clarify whether sort is relevance-first or field-first; don’t silently drop relevance without a control.

11.5 Pagination vs infinite scroll vs load-more

Pattern Prefer when Avoid when
Paged Need item N; SEO; stable address; tables with row actions Casual browse feeds where page breaks feel arbitrary
Load more User-controlled growth; mobile-friendly When users must reach a known position often
Infinite scroll Discovery feeds; low per-item commitment Footer access; task lists; keyboard/AT heavy tables; restoring exact scroll position across sessions

Hard rules:

  • Infinite scroll must not trap keyboard or screen reader users—provide a load-more peer or virtualization with reachable landmarks.
  • Preserve scroll position and selection across back-navigation when possible.
  • Show total count or “approx.” honesty when known; don’t invent precision.
  • For tables, prefer pagination or virtualized window with sticky header—not infinite append that breaks sticky math and “select all.”

11.6 URL persistence & deep links

Shareable views are part of collaboration (Ch. 13). Encode:

  • q query
  • filters (stable keys, not display labels)
  • sort + direction
  • page or cursor

Prefer cursor-based pagination for large mutable sets; page numbers drift when items insert above. When using cursors, the URL still records the cursor token or opaque after param.

Browser Back: returning from a detail page should restore list query/filter/sort/scroll (history state or URL)—not reset to defaults.

11.7 Search + filter zero-state playbook

State Copy skeleton CTA
Empty query, no filters Recent / Suggested / “Search projects” Focus search; optional browse
Query, 0 hits No matches for “X” Clear search; try scope
Filters, 0 hits No items match these filters Clear filters (list chips)
Query + filters, 0 hits Name both constraints Clear search or filters
Error Couldn’t load results Retry
Denied You don’t have access to search here Request access

11.8 Accessibility & performance notes

  • Search field: visible label (not placeholder-only); role="search" landmark where appropriate.
  • Announce result count changes via polite live region (throttle).
  • Debounce network (~150–300ms); cancel in-flight on new keystroke.
  • Keyboard: arrows through results; Enter opens; Esc clears or closes overlay; focus restore on close (L9).

11.9 Chapter 11 summary

  • Build a findability system: search, filter, sort, pagination share one result region and recovery taxonomy.
  • Cmd-K is a palette; search still needs scope, zero honesty, and ranking honesty.
  • Persist refine state in the URL; make filtered-to-zero recoverable.
  • Choose pager vs load-more vs infinite by task—not fashion; always leave an AT-reachable path.

Chapter 12 — Selection, Tables & Drag-and-Drop

Object manipulation is the other half of work: select, inspect, bulk-act, reorder, edit in place. Selection models, data tables/grids, and drag-and-drop were critical or important gaps in the research audit—this chapter supplies the kit.

12.1 Selection models

Model Behavior Prefer when
Single One selected; click replaces Detail inspector; radio-like choice
Multi-toggle Click toggles; Cmd/Ctrl-click add Sparse multi-select
Shift-range Shift-click selects contiguous range from anchor Lists and tables
Scoped select-all Select all in current filter/page/scope—not the entire universe without warning Bulk toolbars
Marquee Drag rectangle (canvas) Design tools; always provide keyboard alt

Rules:

  • Show N selected in a selection-anchored toolbar (Figma-style contextual chrome).
  • Select-all scope must be explicit: “Select all 25 on this page” vs “Select all 1,842 matching filters.” Confirm or progressive disclose the large scope.
  • Clearing filters does not silently clear selection without notice—or does, but announce it.
  • Selection is keyboardable: Space toggles; Shift+Arrow extends; Ctrl/Cmd+A scoped.
  • Empty selection: hide bulk actions; don’t leave destructive buttons enabled at 0.

12.2 Selection-anchored toolbars

When N > 0:

  • Elevate a contextual bar: primary bulk actions + overflow.
  • Keep the bar near the selection or sticky in a predictable place—don’t cover the first selected row’s checkbox.
  • Partial failure on bulk: keep successes; list failures with retry (Ch. 10).
  • Esc clears selection when focus is in the list region (document the shortcut).

12.3 Data tables & grids

Tables are daily-driver density surfaces (prefer density vs air for power users). They need systems, interaction, and a11y contracts—not just <div> rows.

Structure & semantics

  • Use real <table> (or APG grid when cell navigation is required).
  • Column headers with <th> and scope; associate row headers when first column identifies the row.
  • Sticky header on scroll; ensure contrast and focus not clipped.
  • Don’t rely on color alone for status (L11)—text, icon, or pattern too.

Column behaviors

Behavior Spec notes
Resize Drag handle + keyboard resize; persist widths per user
Reorder Drag column or “Move left/right”; announce new order
Show/hide Column picker; don’t remove required identity columns
Pin / freeze Pin identity column on horizontal scroll
Inline edit Enter edits; Esc cancels; Save/blur commits with undo class
Row actions Visible primary; overflow menu; not hover-only on mobile

Keyboard cell navigation (APG grid when needed)

  • Arrow keys move between cells; Home/End; Page Up/Down when virtualized.
  • Enter activates widget inside cell; F2 or Enter for edit mode if spreadsheet-like.
  • Focus visible ≥2px contrast ring; never outline: none.
  • Sortable headers are buttons in the header cell—announced with sort direction.

Loading & empty in tables

  • Skeleton rows matching column layout.
  • Filtered-to-zero inside the table region with chips above—not a marketing empty state.
  • Error row/region with retry; preserve column setup.

Density

Offer comfortable / compact (and dense if daily pro tool) as token maps, not one-off padding. Density toggle is a Superhuman/Gmail-class mechanic—pair with templates for newcomers so density isn’t elitist.

12.4 Drag-and-Drop (DnD)

DnD is high-delight and high-exclusion risk. Ship the pointer path and a peer path.

Concern Requirement
Visible equivalent Buttons/menus: Move up/down, Move to…
Gesture limit ≤1 swipe action per list row; vertical scroll wins
Desktop reorder Prefer explicit handles—don’t make the whole row ambiguous vs click
Drop targets Clear valid/invalid affordance; multi-channel (not color alone)
Keyboard Pick up / move / drop via APG pattern or move dialog
Screen readers Announce grab, position, drop; live region updates
Touch Long-press carefully; don’t break scroll; ≥44×44 handles
Undo Reorder should be soft-undoable when cheap
Reduced motion Instant reposition without fling theater

Prefer-when:

  • Handles for reorderable lists on desktop.
  • Move-to dialog for accessibility and for deep hierarchies where dragging is error-prone.
  • Confirm when drop crosses permission or irreversible boundary.

Reject: hover-only mobile DnD; drag-only merge for sync conflicts (Case H); color-only drop validity.

12.5 Bulk operations checklist

  1. Scope select-all correctly.
  2. Show N selected + blast preview for destructive bulk.
  3. Idempotent server ops where possible.
  4. Partial success UI.
  5. Undo class matches blast (soft vs quarantine vs hard).
  6. Announce completion via polite status; focus remains sensible.

12.6 Chapter 12 summary

  • Selection is a first-class model: shift-range, scoped select-all, selection-anchored toolbar.
  • Tables need semantics, sticky headers, column ops, inline edit, and keyboard maps—not div soup.
  • DnD always ships with a visible keyboard-accessible equivalent; scroll wins; handles beat mystery grabs.

Chapter 13 — Navigation, History, Disclosure, Teaching, Share, Autosave, Clipboard, Notifications & Collab

This chapter covers the “product conversation” around getting to work and staying oriented: where you are, how you got here, what is hidden, how you learn, how you share, how drafts survive, how paste behaves, how alerts interrupt, and how others appear in the same artifact.

13.1 Navigation shells

Platform Chrome bias Must match across platforms?
Web app Side or top nav; Cmd-K Semantics & IA — yes; chrome — no
iOS Tab bar Native chrome — no pixel parity
Android Nav bar / tabs Native chrome

Dual device models—not shrunk desktop (interaction strategy). Shared semantics and tokens; native gestures and materials.

Scent of core action: primary nav labeled until learnability is proven; icon-only primary nav is an anti-pattern. Quiet chrome / loud content on tool surfaces.

Landmarks: skip link to #main; banner, navigation, main, complementary, contentinfo as appropriate; heading outline h1–h6 reflects IA (a11y structure gap).

13.2 History, deep links & Back

  • Every meaningful object view should be addressable (deep link).
  • Browser Back restores prior list refine state (Ch. 11) and focus where feasible.
  • In-app “back” must not fight the browser history stack—prefer real history transitions.
  • Confirm before discarding dirty state if autosave is off; if autosave is on, Back is safe (see 13.6).
  • After modal close, restore focus to the trigger (L9)—history and focus are cousins.

13.3 Progressive disclosure (L8)

Layer Contents Prefer when
Primary Core path actions Must be found without tour
Overflow Secondary actions Frequent enough to need one click
Palette (Cmd-K / /) Long-tail expert actions Power users; dense tools
Settings Rare preferences Not a dumping ground for features

Failure modes: expert dump on the primary surface or buried core action. Disclosure vs discoverability tension: prefer disclosure for long-tail; prefer discoverability for the critical path.

Context menus and hover cards: never the only path to a core action; hover cards need keyboard peer (focus + delay dismiss that is cancellable).

13.4 Teaching & onboarding curriculum

Reject permanent carousels. Prefer a first-artifact curriculum:

  1. Identity — who you are in the product
  2. Artifact — create one real thing (undoable)
  3. Share — invite or publish once
  4. Return cue — reason to come back (notification, bookmark, unfinished draft)

Empty teaching UI (Ch. 10.7) is part of teaching—templates simulate the future (product playbook). Measure time-to-first-value and find-rate of core action without docs.

Help mechanisms: in-context links, short plain language, and searchable help—not a modal wall on first launch. Cognitive: one primary; predictable chrome.

13.5 Share sheets & ACL

Element Spec
Share entry Obvious on artifact; not buried only in “…”
ACL clarity View / comment / edit named in plain language
Link sharing Distinguish invite vs anyone-with-link; warn on wide ACL
Revoke As clear as grant; audit when enterprise
Confirm Hard confirm when widening from private → public

Share is often external irreversibility (notification to others)—bias pessimistic on send, optimistic on copy link with clear ACL badge.

13.6 Autosave & drafts

Pattern Prefer when
Autosave + version history Documents, canvases, long forms
Explicit Save Legal attestations; rare commits; code deploys
Draft + Publish Content that notifies others on publish

UI requirements:

  • Visible save state: Saved / Saving / Offline queued / Error—map to L6 syncing/offline/error.
  • Never lose input on transient error; retry; preserve local draft.
  • Dirty navigation guard only when data would be lost.
  • Conflict with collab: prefer-when keep both / choose / merge (see 13.10 and Ch. 14 offline).

13.7 Clipboard & paste

  • Copy link / copy value: confirm with soft toast (copied).
  • Paste into rich surfaces: sanitize; don’t execute; show paste preview when risky.
  • Paste permissions (web): request on gesture; explain denial (Ch. 14 permissions pattern).
  • Tables: paste grid into cells with clear mapping; undo one paste as a unit.
  • Password fields: allow paste (password-manager-friendly); don’t block clipboard for false security theater.

13.8 Notifications IA

Tier Behavior Prefer when
Critical interrupt Modal or assertive alert Security, payment failure, data loss
Batched digest Center + optional email digest Social, comments, non-urgent
Muteable Per-type mute; quiet hours for non-critical Anything not safety/billing

Notification center: unread clarity; mark-as-read; deep link to object; empty vs zero (no unread vs never used) distinct.

Rules:

  • Toasts queue; don’t stack focus theft.
  • Email/push preference center is part of trust—not a dark pattern maze.
  • In-app badge counts must match reality; don’t invent urgency (growth vs trust tension).

13.9 Wizards & multi-step flows

  • One primary job per step; progress indicator honest (step N of M).
  • Allow Back without wiping; autosave drafts between steps when long.
  • Error Summary on review step; don’t strand users on step 3 with silent invalid step 1.
  • Prefer progressive disclosure over five-page wizards when fields are few.

13.10 Live collaboration

Signal Role
Presence Who is here (Figma-style conversation)
Cursors / following Optional; never required for edit
Comments / threads Anchored to objects; resolve state
Awareness of edits Field-level or region locks when needed
Conflict UI Keep both / choose / merge — keyboard accessible

Prefer-when for conflicts (Case H):

  • Keep both — equal peer edits, unknown merge
  • Choose — one version clearly stale/wrong
  • Merge — structured fields, no overlapping prose

Reject silent overwrite. Announce remote changes politely; don’t steal focus while typing unless destructive collision needs assertive handling.

13.11 Chapter 13 summary

  • Native nav chrome; shared IA; labeled core scent; real deep links and Back.
  • Disclose long-tail; never bury the critical path; teach via first artifact.
  • Autosave makes state talkative; clipboard and share respect ACL honesty.
  • Notifications are tiered and muteable; collab is presence + conflict prefer-when—not ghost edits.

Chapter 14 — Mobile, Gestures, Permissions, Offline & AI UI

Mobile and AI are where interaction strategy meets platform and trust. Dual device models, JIT permissions, offline sync indicators, and AI propose → review → undo are required—not optional polish.

14.1 Dual device models

Concern Shared across devices Native / distinct
Semantic roles, IA, undo classes Yes —
Gestures, nav chrome, materials — Yes
Density defaults Often distinct Comfortable bias on small screens
Hit targets ≥44×44 primary touch —

Reject: pixel-identical RN fantasy; shrunk-web with hover-only actions. Prefer: sheets + buttons on mobile; hover cards demoted.

Safe areas, notches, and foldables: content and sticky actions respect insets; don’t trap CTAs under home indicators.

14.2 Gestures

Rule Detail
≤1 swipe action per list row Competing edges fight scroll
Visible equivalent always Button/menu peer for every gesture
Vertical scroll wins Don’t hijack the main axis casually
Desktop reorder Handles (Ch. 12)
System gestures Respect iOS swipe-back / Android back; don’t override without strong reason
Discoverability Hint once; don’t rely on hidden gestures for core path
Motor a11y No hold-only exclusive path; pointer cancel; adequate spacing

14.3 Permissions (JIT)

Request permission at the moment of intent—not on first app launch in a bundle of scary dialogs.

Step UI
1. User invokes feature needing capability Camera, location, notifications, clipboard, mic
2. Pre-prompt (optional but recommended) Explain value in product UI before OS dialog
3. OS prompt System sheet
4a. Granted Continue task
4b. Denied Explain + link to settings + feature-degraded path—not a dead end

Denied is an L6 state with a CTA (Ch. 10.7). Never loop the OS prompt endlessly; teach how to re-enable.

14.4 Offline & sync

State Show
Offline Banner: “Offline—changes queued” (or read-only honesty)
Syncing Explicit syncing indicator
Synced Quiet; optional last-synced meta
Conflict Both versions + choose/merge/keep both

Case H: reject silent overwrite; keyboard-accessible conflict UI; syncing belongs in the state matrix—not a mystery spinner.

Prefer-when conflicts: keep both (equal peers) · choose (one stale) · merge (structured fields).

Queue mutations optimistically when safe; replay with idempotent keys; surface failures per item.

14.5 AI UI — intent → proposal → review → undo

AI consumes your contract. Ambiguous APIs become industrial defects. Agent UX pattern:

  1. Intent — user asks or triggers a tool
  2. Proposal — streamed output with cancel
  3. Review — diff / citations / preview primary
  4. Apply — explicit
  5. Undo — required
Rule Detail
Stream + cancel Don’t block the UI without an escape
Citations / provenance Show sources when claims matter
Tool side-effects Need approval (email send, delete, purchase)
Diff readable without color Textual +/- or labels; keyboard apply/reject
Trust metric Track reject/override rate—not accept rate alone
Disclosure Label AI-generated content when it matters for trust/safety

Case D — AI bulk edit: Diff primary; stream+cancel; Apply; Undo. Reject autocomplete that silently mutates. Steal Copilot/Cursor apply-review—not ghostwriter theater.

Failure modes: silent AI mutation; optimizing only “accept rate”; red/green-only hunks; unattended agent emails.

14.6 Mobile + AI + offline intersections

  • On flaky networks: stream with reconnect honesty; don’t fake completeness.
  • On mobile: large apply/reject targets; diff in a sheet; don’t require hover for review.
  • Permissions for mic/camera for multimodal AI: JIT + degraded text path.
  • Offline: queue AI requests only if you can fulfill later; otherwise disable with explanation.

14.7 Platform parity snapshot (interaction-relevant)

Concern Web iOS Android Must match?
Semantic color roles ✓ ✓ ✓ Yes
Toast soft-undo duration 5–10s 5–10s 5–10s Yes
Nav chrome Side/top Tab bar Nav bar No — native
Swipe-back Rare System System No — native
Focus ring geometry Focus visible Focus engine Focus engine Intent yes

14.8 Chapter 14 summary

  • Dual models: shared semantics, native gestures/chrome.
  • Gestures never exclusive; JIT permissions with degraded paths.
  • Offline is a designed state with sync and conflict prefer-when.
  • AI is propose → review → apply → undo; side-effects need approval; measure overrides.

Part III Review Questions

Part III Review Questions

A. Feedback, latency, undo & state (Ch. 10)

  1. Write the five phases of the feedback loop and name one failure mode for each.
  2. Give the ≤100ms rule and assign UI patterns to the five latency tiers (instant through long).
  3. When do you choose optimistic vs pessimistic UI? Give one product example of each and the failure if reversed.
  4. Define the three undo classes (soft, quarantine, hard) with durations/mechanisms and a prefer-when for each.
  5. List the seven baseline L6 states. For each, what must the UI show beyond a generic spinner or “No data”?
  6. Taxonomy drill: Distinguish never-used empty, true empty, filtered-to-zero, search zero, error, and denied. Write one headline + one CTA for each for a “Projects” list.
  7. A team uses one empty illustration for both “no projects yet” and “no projects match your filters.” What breaks, and how do you fix it?
  8. Why should toasts rarely steal focus? When is assertive interruption justified?

B. Search, filter, sort & pagination (Ch. 11)

  1. Why is Cmd-K not sufficient as a product search strategy? List at least five requirements of a complete search experience.
  2. Design URL parameters for a shareable filtered table view (query, filters, sort, page/cursor). When would you avoid putting filters in the URL?
  3. Compare pagination, load-more, and infinite scroll with prefer-when / avoid-when. Which is default for an accessible data table, and why?
  4. Write the zero-state matrix for: empty query, query with 0 hits, filters with 0 hits, query+filters with 0 hits, error, denied.
  5. What does “ranking honesty” require when the system applies fuzzy matching?

C. Selection, tables & DnD (Ch. 12)

  1. Explain scoped select-all vs select-everything. Write microcopy for both scopes on a filtered list of 1,842 items with 25 on the page.
  2. Specify keyboard behavior for multi-select with shift-range in a list.
  3. List semantic and interaction requirements for a production data table (headers, sticky, resize, inline edit, loading, filtered-to-zero).
  4. What must every drag-and-drop feature ship alongside the pointer gesture? Give two concrete peer patterns.
  5. Why do desktop reorderable lists prefer handles over whole-row drag?

D. Navigation, history, teaching, share, autosave, clipboard, notifications, collab (Ch. 13)

  1. Map progressive disclosure layers (primary → overflow → palette → settings) and give an example action for each in a project management app.
  2. Outline the four-step first-artifact teaching curriculum. Why reject onboarding carousels?
  3. Autosave vs explicit Save vs Draft/Publish—when is each appropriate? What save states must be visible?
  4. Tier notifications into critical interrupt, batched digest, and muteable. Assign: password reset, new comment, weekly tips, payment failed.
  5. For a sync conflict between two peers editing the same note, which conflict strategy (keep both / choose / merge) do you pick and why?
  6. What ACL information must a share sheet make impossible to miss before “Anyone with the link” is enabled?

E. Mobile, gestures, permissions, offline, AI (Ch. 14)

  1. What is meant by “dual device models, not shrunk desktop”? Name three things that should match across platforms and three that should not.
  2. State the swipe-action rule and the “vertical scroll wins” rule. How do they interact?
  3. Walk through a JIT permission flow including denial with a feature-degraded path (pick camera or notifications).
  4. What offline banner copy and conflict UI does Case H recommend? What is rejected?
  5. Diagram the AI interaction loop: intent → proposal → review → undo. Where do stream+cancel, citations, and tool approval attach?
  6. Why is reject/override rate a better trust metric than accept rate alone for AI apply UX?

F. Integration & critique

  1. Using the Part III laws (L5–L8, L9–L11, L14), critique this flow: User swipes to delete a shared document; no undo toast; confirm dialog says “Are you sure?”; on failure a toast appears and the row is empty/error-ambiguous.
  2. A mobile screen ports a desktop table with hover-only row actions, infinite scroll, and Cmd-Click multi-select only. List five concrete fixes.
  3. Apply craft ∝ trust × frequency: where would you spend the first engineering week—global Cmd-K ranking polish, checkout error recovery, or settings page animation? Justify.
  4. Fill a mini competitive craft scorecard (1–5) for your product vs one rival on: undo honesty, density honesty, core-action scent, and AI review honesty.
  5. Walk the decision cheat-sheet questions “Reversible?” and “AI side effect?” for: (a) archive issue, (b) charge card, (c) agent sends email to customer list.

G. Short design prompts (apply the playbooks)

  1. Spec the empty/zero/error taxonomy for a search results page in an e-commerce inventory admin (including denied and offline).
  2. Design selection + bulk bar + partial failure UI for “Archive 40 issues.”
  3. Write an APG-minded keyboard map for a grid with sortable headers and inline-edit cells.
  4. Specify notification center empty states: never used notifications vs zero unread vs muted-all.
  5. Propose conflict UI wireframe text for offline merge of a structured profile (name, title, bio)—field-level choose vs whole-document choose.

Part III Quick Reference

Topic Bias / number
Acknowledge ≤100ms
Soft undo toast 5–10s
Quarantine ~30d Trash (or product equivalent)
Motion fast / default / slow 100–150 / 150–250 / 300–400ms
Touch target ≥44×44 primary
Feedback loop trigger → ack → work → resolve → undo
Undo classes soft · quarantine · hard
Empty taxonomy never-used · true empty · filtered-to-zero · search zero · error · denied
Findability query · scope · filters · sort · pager + URL
Select-all scoped; show N; warn on match-all
DnD gesture ≤1 swipe; visible + keyboard peer
Notifications critical · digest · muteable + quiet hours
Offline banner + queue + conflict prefer-when
AI stream+cancel · diff · apply · undo · approve side-effects
